findings.title: close() gets a brand-new, universally-required docs-build gate that nothing in the normal lifecycle populates
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:1151-1276 (the `if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS ... "no docs build is recorded" ...` block)
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:312-322 (build() now sets rec["build"] and saves it)
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:923 (build is invoked ONLY from `verb == "build"` in cmd_round — nowhere else)

instruments/check-docs/PROTOCOL.md:57 (unchanged: 'Builds and tests during the pass go through `gbg round build|test <round>`' — described as something done during fixing, not a mandatory pre-close step)
test/rounds.jl:960-967 (round-lifecycle test manually writes r["build"] into ROUND.toml rather than exercising the verb, to make an otherwise-unrelated existing test pass)
findings.before: close() had no build-related precondition at all — the hunk is pure insertion after the existing 'files not committed' check; a check-docs/check-consistency round could close with only the pre-existing checks (git-clean, config-sha, tally, etc.).
findings.after: if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS: b = get(rec, "build", nothing); if b === nothing push!(fails, "no docs build is recorded for this round — gbg round build $round") elseif b["code"] != 0 ... else check staleness via Git.changed_paths(root, "$(b["head"])..HEAD", ...)
findings.why_it_matters: `rec["build"]` is populated ONLY by the `build()` function, which is reached ONLY when a human types `gbg round build <round>` (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:923 is the sole call site — prepare's own inline `run_under_round(cfg, round, cfg["package"]["docs_build"]; log)` calls the raw command, not `Rounds.build`, so it never writes the record). PROTOCOL.md step 4 still describes `gbg round build|test <round>` as something used 'during the pass' when a fix needs verifying, not as a mandatory step for every round regardless of whether a rebuild was ever needed. So a check-docs/check-consistency round that completes prepare → lanes → bank → fix → pass → grade WITHOUT the operator separately invoking `gbg round build` — previously a completely valid, closing lifecycle — is now unconditionally refused at close with no way to satisfy the gate except learning of and running the new verb. The new round-lifecycle test in test/rounds.jl had to hand-inject `r["build"]` directly into ROUND.toml (bypassing `Rounds.build` entirely) to keep an unrelated, pre-existing test passing, which is itself evidence that the natural flow does not produce this record.
findings.description: The commit's own rationale (a red build silently riding through two graded passes) is real and cited (2026-09-12-check-docs-01, work queue), but the fix changes 'the definition of closed' and 'the closure predicates' — both named in §5.5 as non-configurable, MAJOR-to-change invariants — by adding a universal new precondition, without wiring the automatic build step (prepare's inline build) into the same recording path, and without updating PROTOCOL.md to make the new verb a mandatory step. The result is a closure predicate that rejects the previously-valid, undocumented-as-required path of never calling `gbg round build` explicitly.
findings.evidence:
"+    if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS
+        b = get(rec, "build", nothing)
+        if b === nothing
+            push!(fails, "no docs build is recorded for this round — gbg round build $round")" (src/CLI/Passes.jl); "verb == "build" && return build(cfg, round)" is the only call site (src/CLI/Rounds.jl:923); test/rounds.jl:964-967 sets `r["build"] = Dict(...); G.Rounds.save(dir, r)` directly rather than calling `G.Rounds.build`.

findings.title: a partially-anchored seed catalogue escalates from a tolerated, logged skip to a hard refusal, in two call sites, with no test either way
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:161-170 (prepare(), check-consistency branch: new `if !isempty(skipped) ... return 2` before planting)
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:248-257 (seed_docs_corpus!(), check-docs branch: the same new `if !isempty(skipped) ... return 2`)

src/CLI/Rounds.jl:172 (the now-unreachable success-path println still branches on `isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): " * join(skipped, ", ")`, left in place though `skipped` can no longer be non-empty at that point)
findings.before: plan, skipped = Seeds.select(cat, f, rec["seed_salt"]) ... f2, s2 = Seeds.plant(f, s, plan); write(full, f2); write(site, s2); println(io, "prepare: $(length(plan)) seed(s) planted (salt $(rec["seed_salt"]))", isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): " * join(skipped, ", "))
findings.after: plan, skipped = Seeds.select(cat, f, rec["seed_salt"]); if !isempty(skipped) println(io, "prepare: refused — $(length(skipped)) seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript: ", join(skipped, ", ")); ...; return 2 end
findings.why_it_matters: Previously a seed catalogue with one class lacking an anchor in the current corpus still let `gbg round prepare --seed` succeed — it planted the classes that matched and logged which ones it skipped, i.e. a degraded-but-working round. That is exactly the kind of previously-valid input (a partially-stale seed catalogue, plausible as a corpus evolves) this change now hard-refuses for BOTH check-consistency and check-docs rounds. No test in test/rounds.jl, test/seeds.jl or test/gate.jl exercises either the old tolerant path being removed or the new refusal (`grep -rn skipped test/*.jl` finds nothing touching this branch), so the behavior change ships with zero regression coverage in either direction. The leftover dead ternary in the success-path println (line 172) — still written as if `skipped` could be non-empty there — confirms the change was not fully threaded through.
findings.description: The defect motivating this (a skipped class reads as UNDEFINED in recall, silently shrinking the denominator rather than reporting a broken catalogue) is real and well cited, but the fix is a blanket, untested hard-refusal in two call sites rather than, e.g., a warning plus an explicit override — and it is stricter than the pre-existing 'plants nothing at all' refusal it sits beside, which was the only refusal before.
findings.evidence:
"if !isempty(skipped)
                println(io, "prepare: refused — $(length(skipped)) seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript: ", join(skipped, ", "))
...
                return 2
            end" (src/CLI/Rounds.jl, both the check-consistency and check-docs branches, added verbatim in each).

findings.title: a ledger waiver that used to be silently void now silences the entire scan, including hits of rules the consumer never named
locations: src/Scan.jl:706-710 (apply_ledger: `enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id))); for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy") ...`)
test/scans.jl:986-996 (new testset demonstrating a RULE.CIT.DOI-only waiver empties `.hits` for SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK, which also enforces RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE)
findings.before: id = row["id"]; rule = row["rule"]\n    for e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy") ... — only the catalogue's ONE canonical `rule` column could disable the scan via a policy-scope waiver.
findings.after: enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id)))\n    for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy") ... — a policy waiver on ANY rule the scan's `check` array names now disables the scan.
findings.why_it_matters: An existing ledger entry (e.g. `RULE.CIT.DOI`, scope=policy, target=*) that was previously accepted by CFG.EXEMPTIONS and kept live by EXEMPT.STALE, but had NO effect on scanning (it targeted a rule that wasn't the scan's canonical column) now, on upgrade to this version and with no config edit by the consumer, disables the WHOLE scan — including hits under the sibling rule (RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE) the consumer never exempted. The docstring itself calls this 'a known limit... not fixed' because 'a Hit carries no rule id.' This is the audit's core shape: previously-valid, unedited input (the ledger entry) now produces materially different, broader behavior (silently reduced scan coverage on a rule the operator never waived) purely from a tool-version bump.
findings.description: The narrow bug being fixed (a documented waiver that was silently void, defeating the exemption it was meant to grant) is real and well-evidenced, and the residual over-breadth is honestly disclosed as an architectural limit rather than concealed — but the audit still needs it on record because it changes what an unedited, previously-accepted ledger file does.
findings.evidence: "The mirror case is NOT fixed and is a known limit: a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted." (src/Scan.jl docstring); test assertion "r = G.run_scan(d, row; ledger = pol(\"RULE.CIT.DOI\")); @test isempty(r.hits) && r.exempted > 0" (test/scans.jl) shows the DOI-only waiver empties all of the scan's hits.
